definition: Satiate means to satisfy fully or to excess.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word satiate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know satiate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The tasting portions were tiny on purpose: the chef wanted guests intrigued, not satiated, when the main course arrived.
Feed stops short of satiate — feeding answers hunger for now, without promising fullness.
Glut goes further than satiate — to satiate is to fill completely; to glut is to stuff past all pleasure, into queasy excess.

Sate is the blunt old sibling of satiate — to fill someone completely, full stop. Satiate does the same work in a longer robe, and it more readily tips past fullness into too much: a sated guest is done eating; a satiated one may be groaning.

Quench answers thirst specifically — water on a fire, the drink that puts wanting out. Satiate answers hunger and appetite in the broad sense: for food, novelty, or success, filling the want completely until nothing more is asked.
